versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma covers lip (mucosal), buccal mucosa, alveolus, retromolar trigone, floor of mouth, oral tongue and hard palate. The defining 8th-edition change is depth of invasion (DOI): measured from the basement membrane of adjacent normal mucosa to the deepest point of invasion, it upstages small but deeply invasive tumours (5 mm and 10 mm cutoffs) and adds DOI to T1-T3. Extrinsic tongue muscle invasion alone no longer qualifies as T4a; cortical bone invasion does. Nodal staging uses extranodal extension (ENE): clinically overt ENE upstages any node to N3b.

t.label: Tumour 2 cm or smaller with depth of invasion (DOI) 5 mm or smaller
Tumour 2 cm or smaller with DOI larger than 5 mm up to 10 mm, or tumour larger than 2 cm up to 4 cm with DOI 10 mm or smaller
Tumour larger than 4 cm, or any tumour with DOI larger than 10 mm
Moderately advanced disease: invasion through cortical bone, inferior alveolar nerve, floor of mouth, or skin of face (chin/nose); extrinsic tongue muscle invasion alone is not T4a
Very advanced disease: invasion of masticator space, pterygoid plates, skull base, or encasement of internal carotid artery

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Single ipsilateral node 3 cm or smaller, extranodal extension negative (ENE-)
Single ipsilateral node larger than 3 cm up to 6 cm, ENE-
Multiple ipsilateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Bilateral or contralateral nodes 6 cm or smaller, ENE-
Any node larger than 6 cm, ENE-
Any node with clinically overt extranodal extension (ENE+)

versions.regionalNodes: Levels I (submental/submandibular), II (upper jugular), III (mid jugular), IV (lower jugular) and V (posterior triangle); retropharyngeal nodes for posterior lesions. Contralateral or bilateral nodes upstage to N2c.
versions.histologicGrade: Well differentiated (G1), moderately differentiated (G2), poorly differentiated (G3). Worst pattern of invasion (WPOI), perineural and lymphovascular invasion are reported alongside grade.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Conventional squamous cell carcinoma (most cases); verrucous carcinoma (broad pushing front, rarely metastasises); basaloid, papillary, spindle-cell and adenosquamous variants; minor salivary gland carcinomas of the oral cavity use salivary staging.
prognosticFactors: p16 status (prognostic, non-staging in oral cavity)
